articleTitle: Sensor-integrated RIS Unit Element featuring Mutual Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is able to manipulate the propagation of incident electromagnetic waves to form smart radio environments. This paper describes a sensor integrated RIS for optimal 5G communication. The proposed RIS's unit cell consists of via wall to eliminate phase distortion of the sensed signal. In addition, the devised RIS uses varactor diode to change the electric and magnetic properties of the surface in programmable manner and control the wireless channel at 28.0 GHz. Sensing capabilities and beamforming capabilities are verified by 1×4 unit cells configuration. This novel concept is expected to be universally applicable to indoor environment’s blind spot.

articleTitle: A D-band Variable-Gain LNA with Triple-inductive Coupling Gm-boosting
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a D-band frequency variablegain low-noise amplifier (VG-LNA), which is fabricated using a 40 nm RF CMOS process. This designed LNA comprises a 4stage differential amplifiers, and impedance matching is achieved using a transformer. The first stage was designed with a common gate(CG) structure for low noise at high frequency, and sufficient gain was achieved through triple-inductive coupling method. The fourth stage used a cascode structure and common gate cross summing method for high gain and stable gain control function. It shows a gain of 21.2 dB and a noise Figure of 8.1 dB at 148 GHz. The measured minimum $I P_{1 d B}$ is −28.5 dBm and gain control range is 12.5 dB at 148 GHz. The total area of the chip, including the pads, is $0.24\mathrm{~mm}^2$, and the chip consumes 41 mW of DC power.

articleTitle: Microstrip Line Non-Reciprocal Bandpass Filter With Tunable Center Frequency
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a design of a magnet-less microstrip line non-reciprocal bandpass filter (BPF) with tunable center frequencies. The proposed non-reciprocal BPF uses quarter-wavelength time-modulated resonators. To achieve a non-reciprocal (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>|≠|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>|) filter response, a progressive phase shift AC modulation signal is applied to varactors through transmission line, which simplifies the modulation scheme. The center frequency is tuned by changing dc-bias voltage of varactor diode. For experimental validation, a prototype has been designed and fabricated. The measured results confirmed that center frequency is tuned from 1.45 GHz to 1.55 GHz with forward insertion loss variation of 3.71 dB to 3.40 dB and reserve isolation is higher than 10 dB.

articleTitle: 29-to-65-GHz CMOS Amplifier with Tunable Frequency Response
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In the 300-GHz band, a very wide bandwidth of up to 44GHz is available for wireless communications. This paper presents a frequency-response tunable CMOS IF amplifier, intended for 300-GHz wireless communications. It could be used for frequency-domain equalization at IF. The amplifier was fabricated using a 40-nm CMOS process. 3-dB bandwidth of 36GHz and power gain of 27.3dB are obtained at a power consumption of 144mW.

articleTitle: Investigation of BEoL integrated ferroelectric thin-film HfO2 for mmWave varactor applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate Back-End-of-Line (BEoL) integrated thin-film varactors based on ferroelectric hafnium zirconium oxide. We furthermore show the implementation of such novel metal-ferroelectric-metal (MFM) thin-film varactors in a passive delay-line phase shifter at millimeter wave frequencies. Upon the frequencies up to 67 GHz and a small voltage range of -3V to 2V, the device has demonstrated the phase shift of 43.5° at 45 GHz with an insertion loss (IL) of 14 dB, and 112 ° at 60 GHz with an IL of -41.3 dB. The device area is 0.512 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding the pads. Its exceptional CMOS compatibility, making it suitable for all major CMOS and BiCMOS technologies, and its low-voltage operation make it a promising candidate for a wide range of microwave and millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A High Gain Vector-Sum Phase Shifter in 28-nm CMOS for 5G communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a high gain vector-sum phase shifter for mmWave communication in a 28 nm CMOS process. The proposed phase shifter consists of an input matching network (IMN) with cascode structure, a coupler type I/Q generator, a variable gain amplifier (VGA), and an output matching network (OBN). The different loaded coupler is utilized in the I/Q generator to obtain a quadrature signal. To increase the gain of the phase shifter, the transistors and capacitors connected with the coupler are optimized. Moreover, the cascode topology is utilized in IMN to implement high isolation as well as enhancement of the gain. The Gilbert cell design is applied to control the I/Q signal in the VGA. The proposed phase shifter achieves a phase shift of 4-bits with high gain in the 32.5 - 36.5 GHz band. The maximum average gain is -1.65 dB at 34.5 GHz, and the root-mean-square (RMS) phase error of 2.24° and RMS gain error of 0.59 dB with power consumption is 27 mW from a 1.8-V supply. The proposed vector-sum phase shifter achieves a high gain with an I/Q generator in Ka-band.

articleTitle: 100GHz-Band On-Chip 1x2 Phased Array Antenna Fed By Hybrid Coupler On 45nm CMOS SOI
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 100GHz-band $1\times 2$ beam steering array antenna based on 45nm CMOS silicon on insulator technology of high resistivity $2500\Omega$.cm. An inset-fed patch antenna is designed as the radiating element. The maximum simulated gain is 5.8dBi at 100GHz. A 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> Branch Line Hybrid Coupler is designed as the Beamforming Network (BFN). To miniaturize the design, the BFN is inserted into the ${\lambda}_{0}$/2 inter-space between the two antenna elements. The concept is demonstrated in the 80-120GHz bandwidth with a $1\times 2$ array, achieving a simulated 7.5dBi maximum realized gain and ±22<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> beam scan angles in 1-D. The measurement of the return losses shows good agreement with the simulations. The array antenna’s total chip area is 2.548mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: 25-31-GHz Low Noise Amplifiers in 0.15-µm GaN/SiC HEMT Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents two 25-31GHz LNAs in $0.15- \mu$ maN/SiC HEMT process. The proposed 2-stage CS LNA exhibits 15-17 dB gain with 2.4-3.1 dB NF, $17.4\mathrm{dBm}OP_{1dB}$ and $24.2\mathrm{dBm}\mathrm{OHP}_3$. In comparison, the proposed CS+Cascode LNA with a 15-18 dB gain and 2.2-2.8dB NF has only limited linearity of $5.2\mathrm{dBm}OP_{1dB}$ and $13.3 \mathrm{dBm}OP_{3}$. Both LNAs consume 0.3 W dc power and with a chip area of $1.4\times0.6 \mathrm{mm}^2$.

articleTitle: Optimization of Deep Learning-Based BSIM-CMG I-V Parameter Extraction in Seconds
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A deep learning-based parameter extraction for industry standard BSIM-CMG compact model is presented in this paper. A Monte-Carlo simulation varying key BSIM-CMG parameters was performed to create the 1 million I-V sweep data for training. A deep Learning model is trained with drain current I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">D</inf> as an input and the BSIM-CMG parameters as the output. The trained neural network was able to successfully model TCAD I-V data. The results show very promising capability of the deep learning-based parameter extraction to develop compact models within seconds with less or comparable error compared to traditional manual parameter extraction.

articleTitle: Multiplexing Schemes for sub-THz/THz Interconnects (Invited)
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper discusses the multiplexing schemes for sub-THz/THz Interconnect, which has the potential to complement the existing electrical and optical interconnects. Using a wideband and low-loss Si dielectric waveguide (DWG) as the medium, the proposed sub-THz/THz interconnect achieves tens of Gbps date rates with high energy-efficiency with the potential to reach a longer distance than electrical interconnects. The bandwidth density can be further boosted by employing advanced multiplexing schemes. Frequency division, mode division and polarization multiplexing are discussed and demonstrated. The simulated and measured results show that the multiplexing schemes expand the transmission bandwidth by introducing multiple sub-channels with crosstalk <-20 dB.

articleTitle: Two-stage CMOS/GaAs HBT Doherty Power Amplifier Module for 5G Handsets
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage Doherty power amplifier module (PAM) in CMOS SOI and GaAs HBT technologies for 5G handsets. While the driver amplifier is implemented using SOI CMOS for low cost, the carrier and peaking amplifiers are implemented using InGaP/GaAs HBT for high efficiency and linearity. The proposed Doherty PAM has a differential driver whose two output terminals are connected to the input ports of the carrier and peaking amplifiers, respectively. For the 3.35 GHz continuous-wave (CW) signal, the proposed PAM exhibited a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 30.3% and a power gain of 29.8 dB at a peak output power of 32.2 dBm. Using the 5G New Radio (NR) signal with a peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of 9.7 dB and a signal bandwidth of 100 MHz, a linear gain of more than 19.5 dB and a linear output power of more than 17 dBm in the range of from 3.15- to 4.15 GHz with a supply voltage of 4.5 V.

articleTitle: A Compact Mm-Wave Multi-Band VCO Based on Triple-Mode Resonator for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We present a low phase noise four-core triple-band voltage controlled-oscillator (VCO) with reconfigurable oscillator cores and multi-mode resonator. By activation/deactivation of oscillator cores and change of resonator impedance in three modes of operations, the proposed VCO provides complete freedom in selecting the resonance frequency for three operation bands in the mm-wave range. The proposed four-core triple-band VCO is implemented in a 65 nm CMOS process using a compact high-Q triple-mode resonator. The VCO oscillation frequencies center at 19,28, and 38 GHz while providing good phase noise and low power consumption in all bands. Measured results show the total frequency tuning range (FTR) of 38.5% while the PN at 1MHz offset varies from −100.3dBc/Hz to −106.06 dBc/Hz resulting in an excellent $\mathrm{FoM}_{\mathrm{T}}$ of 199.8 dBc/Hz.

articleTitle: 23-28 GHz Doherty Power Amplifier Using 28 nm CMOS for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a Doherty power amplifier (DPA) designed to operate at the 23 – 28 GHz frequency band for 5G applications. The load network was designed by converting a transmission line-based DPA network to an equivalent transformer-based matching network. Broadband characteristics of the load network was achieved through balancing the impedance transformation ratio at the matching networks of the carrier and peaking amplifiers. The DPA was fully integrated with the 28 nm bulk CMOS process. The designed DPA exhibited gain of 14.0 – 18.5 dB, saturated output power of 11.9 – 12.3 dBm, peak power-added efficiency (PAE) of 19.4 – 26.0%, and PAE of 12.8 – 14.3% at 6 dB output power backoff (OBO) when measured with a continuous wave (CW) signal.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz Electromagnetic-Wave Absorber for Future Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Sub-terahertz (Sub-THz) frequencies are a promising frequency band for ultra-high-speed data communication in the future. D-band frequencies are one of them for beyond 5G/6G communication from 2030. To realize it, a method by employing an electromagnetic-wave (EM) absorber to suppress the cavity resonance at those frequencies and to increase reliability has been required at the module-fabrication level. In this work, we show an ultra-wideband D-band EM absorber based on the measurement results of dielectrics.

articleTitle: A 57-64 GHz Two-Way Parallel-Combined Power Amplifier with 16.6 dBm Psat and 23.6% Peak PAE in 40nm Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient and linear two-way parallel-combined CMOS power amplifier (PA). A pair of over-neutralization cross-coupled capacitors are used to boost the power gain and ensure stability. Design-oriented analysis leads to the optimum efficiency of the transformers in the power combiner, and the dummy-shielding winding is applied to improve the load impedance uniformity seen by each PA cell. Fabricated in a 40 nm CMOS process, the P A achieves 23.6 % peak power added efficiency (PAE), 16.6 dBm saturated output power $\left(P_{\text {sat }}\right)$, and 14.6 dBm output 1-dB compression point $\left(\mathrm{P}_{1dB}\right)$ with 20.5 % PAE. The peak PAE is above 20 % and $P_{\text {sat }}$ is above 15 dBm across 57-64 GHz frequency range. P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1dB</inf> exceeds 14 dBm from 59 GHz to 64 GHz.

articleTitle: Vital Signal Detection for Continuous-Wave Radar Sensor using Compensation Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A beam-controllable radar sensor and its signal processing are proposed for improving sensitivity in vital signal detection caused by static clutters. The main beam direction of the continuous-wave radar sensor is adjusted by controlling the single-pole single-thru (SPST) RF switches configured in the series patch antenna array. The periodic change of the radar beam direction generated by continuously controlling the switches causes modulated signals at the baseband. The vital signals can be extracted from the separated baseband signals by the envelope detection method. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the vital signals is increased from the processing gain of the modulated signals by using the cross-correlation technique including the detrending method. Experimental results showed that the SNRs of respiration and heartbeat detection were increased by 5.2 dB and 6.6 dB, respectively, by beam switching and signal processing of the proposed radar sensor.

articleTitle: Grating Lobe Suppression in Wide-Angle Scanning Phased Array with Large Inter Element Spacing by Subarray Rotation
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The use of mmWave and THz is required in wireless communication according to the advantages of broadband use. The scanning range of the phased array is limited by grating lobes caused by the antenna elements’ interval increase. Antenna element intervals where grating lobes do not occur are physically small according to high frequencies, so it is small compared to chip size and difficult to manufacture. The grating lobe was reduced by arranging a subarray composed of 4 × 4 antenna elements having an interval of 1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. By reducing the grating lobe by giving spacing between subarrays and rotating the subarrays, the sidelobe level is as low as -10dB or less. The proposed phased array antenna arrangement has a large interval between antenna elements and does not overlap between subarrays, so it is easy to manufacture and achieves a low sidelobe level even during steering.

articleTitle: A 350-GHz Fundamental-Mode Common-Base Cross-Coupled Oscillator in 130-nm InP HBT Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 350-GHz fundamental-mode oscillator with a common-base cross-coupled topology has been developed based on a 130-nm InP HBT technology. A fabricated oscillator with a typical performance showed an oscillation frequency of 344 GHz. The measured output power was 1.1 dBm with a DC power dissipation of 74.8 mW, leading to a DC-to-RF efficiency of 1.72 %. It was confirmed from the measurement that a base inductance of 4 pH (for a device size of 5-$\mu$m emitter length) needs to be included for accurate prediction of the circuit performance, which would serve a useful guideline for circuit designs with the given process technology.

articleTitle: A Refined Skew Matrix Model of the CIM3 in the Up-Mixer Extending the Duality of I/Q Imbalance
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a refined nonlinear I/Q im-balance model that includes the intermodulation terms missed in our prior work on the mathematical model of the up-mixer impairments proposed then. Based on this late correction mainly extending the duality of I/Q imbalance to CIM3, a more physically plausible model and consistent results were obtained, while maintaining the framework of a single skew matrix representation for joint compensation and estimation of I/Q imbalance and CIM3.

articleTitle: Deep Learning enabled mmWave PA and Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Future mmWave and THz wireless chip-scale systems need to be incorporate complex functionalities including ability to operate over multiple spectral bands in an agile fashion spread across 30-100+ GHz, support spectrum sharing and concurrent multi-band transmission, and allow joint sensing and communication. Design methodologies to enable such challenging features typically suffer from tradeoffs across energy efficiency, bandwidth, linearity and reconfigurability. These trade-offs arise from multiple domains, and primarily from the fact that enabling such features through carefully designed electromagnetic structures, taken from a library of templates, invariantly trades off with loss and efficiency. In this paper, we demonstrate how deep-learning based techniques can allow on-demand rapid synthesis of complex passives structures and antennas. These passive elements are not limited to a library of templates, and therefore, can enable functionalities beyond the capability of human intuition and design insights. Combined with circuits, we demonstrate a deep learning based mmWave PA with 30-94+ GHz P_sat,3dB bandwidth, while supporting concurrent multiband transmission for the first time at mmWave. We also demonstrate how this can enable rapid antenna designs with desired characteristics for these high frequency systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband Power Amplifier Covering 23-39 GHz for 5G Mobile Communication
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage broadband power amplifier (PA) for fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication. For simultaneous broadband performance in small-signal gain, saturated output power $(\mathrm{P}_{\text{sat}})$ and 1-dB compression output power $(P_{\text{laB}})$, a leakage inductor and a shunt capacitor are added in output matching network and a weakly-coupled transformer is adopted in inter-stage matching network. Implemented in 65 nm CMOS process, this PA achieves peak gain of 18. dB with 3-dB small-signal gain bandwidth from 23 to 39GHz(51.6%), 1-dB $P_{\text{sat}}$ bandwidth from 23.9 to 38.1 GHz(45.8%) and I-dB

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized High-gain Patch Antenna Using Higher-order Mode for GPS Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a circularly polarized high-gain patch antenna for GPS applications. The CP radiation pattern is theoretically obtained by summing E-fields of $\mathrm{TM}_{030}^{x}$ and $\mathrm{TM}_{003}^{x}$ modes with a phase difference of 90°. To verify the design obtained based on the cavity model theory, we fabricate and measure the proposed antenna. The measured and simulated reflection coefficients are less than −13.3dB at 1.7 GHz. In addition, the measured and simulated bore-sight gains are 9.9 dBic and 10.6 dBic, respectively.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave/THz CMOS Phased-Array Transceiver for 5G and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this presentation, a 28-GHz phased-array transceiver and 300GHz transceiver realized by 65nm CMOS will be introduced, which are designed for 5G and beyond. The talk concludes with a discussion on future directions of millimeter-wave wireless communication.

articleTitle: A 28-GHz Low Insertion Loss Variation 4-Bit Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a 28 GHz low insertion loss variation 4-bit phase shifter which cover 360° phase. The phase shifter is implemented using 28-nm CMOS process. The phase shifter is based on switched delay type phase shifter topology. In order to reduce the insertion loss imbalance, it is designed so that resonance admittance that caused by shunt inductor and parasitic capacitance of off state shunt switching transistor is the same as on resistance of shunt switching transistor. The Fabricated 4-bit phase shifter has 10.1° RMS phase error and 0.78 dB RMS insertion loss at the center frequency. The lowest RMS phase error is 6.4° at 25 GHz and the lowest RMS insertion loss error is 0.18 dB at 30 GHz. The measured insertion loss is 11.7 ± 2.4dB from 28 to 31 GHz over all 16 states.

articleTitle: 900 MHz Differential Power Amplifier IC Using 55 nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a differential power amplifier integrated circuit (PAIC) based on the 55 nm Complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) process for the 900 MHz band. The two-stage CMOS PA was designed to have optimized efficiency and linearity using second-harmonic control circuits at the source and drain of the main stage. RC feedback and cross-coupled capacitor were adopted for stabilization. The implemented PAIC delivers the linear gain of more than 25 dB and the output power of more than 27.2 dBm at the center frequency of 900 MHz.

articleTitle: A Switchless Bidirectional Distributed Amplifier with 2-dB Gain Variation in One Decade Frequency Range in 90-nm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a switchless bidirectional distributed amplifier (BDDA). The proposed BDDA is implemented using a skew-symmetric layout in 90 nm CMOS technology. The BDDA achieves a flat gain within the desired frequency range which is benefit from the skew-symmetric layout. The measured gain variation is 2 dB from 3 to 30 GHz with a peak small-signal gain of 13.8 dB. The 3-dB bandwidth is 31.5 GHz and the circuit consumes a dc power of 45.8 mW. The BDDA occupies an area of 0.93 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Design of Power Detector for mm-Wave Beamforming Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A CMOS power detector is proposed for power monitoring of transceivers in mm-Wave beamforming systems. The power detector outputs a voltage in a log-linear relationship with respect to the RF input power. To improve voltage response at low RF input power, the transistor is designed to operate in the sub-threshold region. The proposed power detector has a linear output voltage response characteristic with a slope of −20 mV/dB for RF input signal power in the range of −15 dBm to 11 dBm. For frequencies above 10 GHz, the log-linearity dynamic range of the power detector is 26 dB, with a log-linearity error within ± 1 dB in this range. The proposed power detector can be used to monitor the output signal strength of the transmit/receive channel in the mm-Wave beamforming system.

articleTitle: Mm-wave CMOS Matrix Distributed Amplifier for Ultra-Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents an mm-wave CMOS matrix distributed amplifier (matrix-DA) exhibiting an ultra-wide bandwidth. The amplifier consists of multi-tiered DAs and an on-chip inductive bias network. The distributed line length is optimized for dealing with a tradeoff between the impedance matching and bandwidth. The output signals from each gain cell are coherently added by adopting the group-delay equalization technique. Peaking lines are inserted at the interstage network to increase the gain-bandwidth product (GBP). The experimental results show that a nominal gain of 6.2 dB and a 3-dB bandwidth of 70 GHz is achieved. The GBP reaches 142.9 GHz. The return loss is higher than 10 dB over the entire 3-dB bandwidth. The chip size is 0.81 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction for Target Classification Using an FMCW Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents a preprocessor for classification of FMCW radar signal processing. Since the start position and the speed are different for each target, the classification accuracy can be improved by calibrating the distance and the timing for the target image. Thus, the size and start timing of the echo signal was corrected through the proposed preprocessor. To verify the proposed preprocessor, a hand gesture recognition system environment was built. The performance evaluation results showed that the gesture recognition accuracy for the five gestures was measured to be 91.5% in a user-independent manner.

articleTitle: An Accurate and Instantaneous Permittivity Measurement Using Modified Multi-line Method
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper describes an extended permittivity extraction technique based on the Multi-line method. The proposed method consists of (1) two CPW lines with different lengths and (2) material under test (MUT). It can be applicable to rapid and wideband characterization of dielectric constants without additional fabrication or extensive measurement setups. The investigated results of three known materials (Teflon, Taconic RF-35, Glass) confirms the validity of the proposed permittivity extraction method. These results exhibit a broadband operation capability from 0.3 GHz to 35.0 GHz with the averaged accuracy of 95.0%.

articleTitle: Differential HPUE PA for n77 Band with a Cross-Coupled Feed-Forward Gain Control Circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A differential PA (power amplifier) compatible with HPUE (high power user equipment) of n77 band for 5G portable terminals was prototyped. Not only the gain, efficiency, and linear characteristics of HPM (high power mode), the characteristics of LPM (low power mode) are also important. In this paper, we propose CCFF (cross-coupled feed-forward) gain control circuits as power mode switching circuits suitable for differential PA. The CCFF gain control circuit does not require BiFET (bipolar and field effect transistor) or CMOS (complementally metal oxide semiconductor) integrated circuit for switch integration. It can be easily realized only with HBT (hetero bipolar transistor), with a small circuit scale. By this proposed configuration, a gain difference of 15 dB or more was realized between HPM and LPM, and VSWR (voltage standing wave ratio) <2.0 were achieved both HPM and LPM.

articleTitle: Correction of Multilayer Semiconductor Process Parameters for Electromagnetic Field Analysis in the 300-GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In order to correct the process parameters of multilayer semiconductor processes and to achieve accurate electromagnetic field analysis in the terahertz band, we propose a method and present a procedure that can determine the thickness of dielectric layers and metal thickness separately, which is not possible using conventional process parameter correction methods. To validate the proposed method, two types of transmission lines and one type of metal-oxide-metal (MOM) capacitor were fabricated using a 0.13 μm SiGe BiCMOS process and by using the process parameters corrected by the proposed method, we show that the results of electromagnetic field analysis and measurements are in good agreement at 300 GHz.

articleTitle: An Ultra-compact Bidirectional Ka-Band Front-End Module with 4.0-dB NF and 13.5-dBm OP1dB
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-compact bidirectional Ka-band front-end module (FEM) by using foldedtransformer-based matching networks and transformer-based transmit/receive switches (TRSWs). This design uses 8-shaped folded transformer technique to cancel the magnetic coupling enabling transmit path can be folded to the receive path and the matching networks of power amplifier (PA) and low noise amplifier (LNA) can share a same footprint, which improves the area efficiency greatly with negligible performance penalty. Furthermore, the TRSW, which is composed of a three-inductor coupled resonator, realizes the functions of the balun, input matching network of the receiver (RX), and output matching network of the transmitter (TX) within only an inductor footprint. Implemented in 65-nm CMOS process, the FEM achieves 26 dB peak gain with a 4.0 dB minimum NF in RX mode, while it achieves peak gain of 26.5 dB and 15.1 dBm saturated output power (Psat) in TX mode in Ka-band. The core size of this proposed design is only 0.1 mm2 that is only 20% to 50% of the size occupied in prior works.

articleTitle: A study of K-band gain-boosted amplifier using inductor coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: To obtain a high-gain amplifier in the high-frequency band, such as K-band, this paper studies a circuit with inductor coupling based on a cascode amplifier. The core circuit of the amplifier consists of a source inductor connected to the source side of a cascode transistor and a gate inductor connected to the gate side. The measurement results showed that the gain of 16.8 dB at20 GHz, and the maximum gain of 18.7 dB at 18.9 GHz, confirming that a high gain can be obtained in the K-band. The process used was the TSMC 0.1S$\mu$m CMOS process.

articleTitle: Power Combining Configurations of HPUE PA for 5G Mobile Phone Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: With the spread of 5G (5th generation) mobile phones, increasing the output power of PAs (power amplifiers) will become an important issue. From the viewpoint of power combining, a differential PA capable of increasing the output voltage amplitude is attracting attention. In the case of differential operation, it is possible to set a load impedance four times that of a single-ended PA with the same output power, which reduces the loss due to the parasitic resistance of the OMC (output matching circuit) and at the same time realizes a wider matching bandwidth. The transformer matching circuits have been widely studied as a matching circuit suitable for differential PA. The transformer matching circuit can easily realize differential/single conversion. For this reason, transformer matching circuits are an essential technology for differential PAs. In this report, we compare typical power combining configurations and clarify the advantages of differential PA. We also compared the matching bandwidth of the CL-LC matching circuits with the basic transformer matching circuits in which the input/output shunt capacitance is added to the transformer. As a result, it was shown that although the matching bandwidth of the transformer matching circuits are slightly narrowed, it is possible to realize a matching bandwidth that is comparable to the CL-LC matching circuits.

articleTitle: Design of Diplexer-matching Dual-band Active Load Mixer with Master-Slave IF Active Filter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: The proposed design is a low-power dual-frequency active load mixer with master-slave intermediate frequency active filter applied to 2.4GHz (ISM-Band) /5.7GHz (U-NII band). The measured results of mixer adopt the conversion gain of 12dB, the noise index of 14.5dB, and the IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> of −6.9dBm at 2.4GHz; the conversion gain of 14.5dB, the noise index of 10.3dB, and the IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> of −6.9dBm at 5.7GHz. Using LC-tank to filter the output harmonic of mixer. Negative resistor compensation circuit can propose optimized Q of LC-tank. Using the $\text{V}_{\text{control}}$ of VCO in PLO can finetune the center frequency of the filter. The experimental of filter present the noise Figure of 11.8dB, input P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ldB</inf> of −23dBm and the IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> of – 14dBm at 3dB attenuation from 0dB and 20MHz bandwidth. After gain adjustment, the noise Figure of 21dB, input P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ldB</inf> of – 10dBm and IIP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> of −7dBm at input loss of 10dB. The power consumption of 6.8/ 7.4mW at 2.4/ 5.7GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Cooperative Microwave Power Transfer using Beam Scanning Scheme
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a beam scanning scheme for cooperative microwave power transfer. Two transmitters and a receiver operate based on a frame consisting of a scanning slot and an energy transfer slot. Transmitters transmit pilot signals in sub-slots of scanning slots, and receivers feedback the index at which the maximum rectified DC voltage is measured, thereby acquiring information necessary for cooperative microwave power transfer. Through the acquired information, the transmitters steer the beam toward the receiver while causing constructive interference at the position of the receiver to increase the received power. To verify the proposed scheme, two 5.8 GHz 16-channel digital beamforming systems were implemented.

articleTitle: Research of Dual-Path DC-DC Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper shows a DC-DC power converter with dual current flows, which is called a dual-path converter. It has a hybrid structure using a flying capacitor to make an additional current path apart from an inductor as an energy transfer media. In conventional approaches with a single current path, the parasitic resistance in series with the inductor causes significant conduction loss. However, thanks to the reduction of the dc level of the inductor current of the converter, the dual-path converter shows higher efficiency than the conventional DC-DC converter. Also, since this structure allows a small-sized inductor and a capacitor, the volume of the power management module can be reduced to be adopted to various IoT devices and it can reduce the manufacturing cost. The measurement results of the prototypes verified the advantages of the dual-path power converter.

articleTitle: A 4-9 GHz Reconfigurable Differential Power Combiner/Splitter in 65nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a 4-9 GHz reconfigurable differential power combiner/splitter in a 65nm CMOS process is presented for the phased array communication. With cross-coupled transistor pair, the single-pole single-throw (SPST) switch is realized with high isolation and linearity performance. For interconnecting purpose, a differential grounded shielded CPW (GSCPW) is introduced for low insertion loss and high isolation performance. The measurement results show that the insertion loss of the power combiner/splitter, including the Balun, SPST and GSCPW, is about -10.7dB at 6 GHz. Moreover, the SPST has an isolation of more than 40 dB.

articleTitle: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output-Beam Mixing Radar for Fast Sweeping Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a new concept for high-frame-rate mixing radar application. This radar consists of two transmitters and one receiver. By using Multiple-Input Multiple-Output-Beam concept, the output power of the transmitters can focus on individual 4 beam directions simultaneously and provide sufficient power for the transponder to perform mixing function. In the receiver, a digital beamforming technique is used to to perform a sweep in one data acquisition. For the verification, a 9.3/9.5 GHz mixing radar is built and tested. In the indoor testing, this radar can achieve 22 frames per second. Compared to the published radar for small species tracking, this radar has the highest frame rate and is expected to be able to capture the transient instant flight trajectory of bees.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency-Reconfigurable Filtering Phase Shifter Based on Controllable Mixed Electric-Magnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Bandpass filter and phase shifter are both crucial devices in modern wireless communication systems. Integration design of these two standalone blocks can bring numbers of benefits to system such as lowering the insertion loss, reducing circuit size, etc. On the other hand, enabling the center frequency tunability of these devices can further improve the flexibility of system, making it available for various applications under different communication standards. This paper presents a short review of our recently proposed works on frequency-reconfigurable filtering phase shifter (FPS). Design methods for different types of frequency-reconfigurable FPS are introduced. The corresponding circuit prototypes and measured results are also presented.

articleTitle: Design of a High-gain Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Using Periodic Diagonal Slots and an Elliptical Director for Microwave Power Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-gain Antipodal Vivaldi antenna operating in the ISM bands of 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz for microwave power transmission systems. The proposed antenna is composed of an antipodal Vivaldi antenna the two radiating flares, periodic diagonal slots, and an elliptical director to improve the bandwidth and the bore-sight gain. The simulated bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 75% with a center frequency of4 GHz. The bore-sight gains are 8.4 dBi at2.4 GHz and 11.8 dBi at 5.8 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Metasurface Scheme using Polarization Matching for Improving Resource Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for efficient resource utilization. The proposed method makes efficient use of resources by adaptively applying polarization matching (PM) using the polarization information of users. Since the increasing transmission power of 6G communication with extreme path loss imposes environmental issues and hardware burden, the transmission power needs to be used efficiently. Multi-beam metasurface (MBM) using PM enables efficient use of transmit power by reducing unnecessary resource use. Formulas and guidelines for the proposed method are presented to aid understanding and simulated at 140GHz for verification. The proposed method can be considered to improve resource efficiency in 6G communication.

articleTitle: A Mm-Wave CMOS Feed-Forward Amplifier Based on a Quasi-Balanced Structure
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a linearized millimeter-wave amplifier implemented in a 65-nm CMOS technology. A feedforward linearization technique was adopted to a quasi-balanced amplifier which separates the signal and intermodulation distortions. After the feed-forward linearization, the output third order intercept point (OIP3) of the proposed amplifier with three amplifier core is improved by 8 dB comparing to the single core amplifier.

articleTitle: An Energy-Efficient Supply- and Temperature-Independent ΔΣ Capacitance-to-Digital Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Capacitance-to-digital converters (CDCs) are widely used for measuring pressure, humidity and acceleration [1–3] in a myriad of biomedical and IoT applications, where energy-efficiency and robustness against supply and temperature variations are of paramount importance. For instance, a wirelessly powered device will need to maintain its sensing accuracy in the presence of a varying supply voltage festered with digital switching noise. On the other hand, stand-alone IoT devices may need to sense variables accurately in varying ambient temperatures and battery supply voltage levels. In both cases, energy efficiency is a key requirement to sustain long-term device operation from a battery. Given the stringent limitations on the form-factor, such systems often need to employ small-sized, low-sensitivity sensors, necessitating the CDC to have a high sensing resolution. Among the previously proposed CDCs, the SAR-CDC [1] achieves high-energy efficiency. However, its input bridge is directly dependent and hence sensitive to supply voltage variations and supply-noise. Secondly, the resolution is only ∼6fF, despite the high energy efficiency. Several recent works have adopted time-domain CDCs employing a VCO quantizer to achieve high-resolution at low power. A SAR-VCOΔΣ CDC [2] reported high energy efficiency along with ∼1fF resolution that needed calibration to maintain accuracy followed by a closed-loop two-step SAR-TDΔΣ CDC [3] avoided the need for calibration. Still, these architectures are susceptible to supply and temperature effects, especially when they vary over a wide range. To solve these issues, we propose a time-locked ΔΣ CDC (TLΔΣ CDC) w hose output is derived from a VCO w hose period is locked to a precise external clock TREF. Furthermore, the VCO is time-locked by regulating its local supply and ground, making it insensitive against any variations in the chip-level supply. Multi-bit counters are used for the generation of the output, with the aim to reduce the time-quantization error and reduce the overall power by lowering the sampling frequency. As a result, the proposed TLΔΣ CDC can achieve the state-of-the-art FOMS=2.54μJ∙ppm2, supply sensitivity of ±0.55%/V over 1.2-2.2V and temperature sensitivity of 49.1ppm/°C over -20°C and 125°C. The sensing resolution is 70.5aF. Implemented in a 0.18μm standard CMOS process, the TLΔΣ CDC consumes 42.76μW from a 1.2V supply and 0.2mm2 active area.

articleTitle: Design of waveguide-based H-band source module using InP HBT integrated circuits
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present an H-band source module in a WR-3 rectangular waveguide. An H-band amplifier and frequency multiplier integrated circuits (ICs) are designed in a 250 nm InP HBT technology. Waveguide-to-microstrip transitions based on dipole antenna are also designed and used to mount the fabricated ICs in the waveguide. The design issues concerned with the waveguide package are also discussed in the paper with the measurement results.

articleTitle: Study on Loss of Varactor-Loaded Tunable Microstrip Antennas Considering Q Factor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, loss of a varactor-loaded frequency tunable antenna is investigated. The gain degradation of the antenna due to conductor loss, dielectric loss, and varactor loss cannot be ignored. We calculate the Q factors of the antenna to evaluate each loss and investigate its loss mechanism.

articleTitle: Design of wideband CMOS ESD protection circuit using mutually coupled inductor
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we present a wideband electrostatic discharge (ESD) protection circuit in a 28 nm FDSOI CMOS process. The diodes used in the ESD protection circuit introduce the large parasitic capacitance in the IO pads which seriously limits the IO bandwidth of the high-speed CMOS circuits. In order to compensate for the parasitic capacitance and restore the bandwidth, mutually coupled inductor are proposed using the stacked metal layers in CMOS process. It allows the tighter magnetic coupling and more freedom in the design than the conventional T-coil. Therefore, it can lead to the high ratio of bandwidth extension under a compact chip area. The proposed circuit was fabricated in a 28 nm FDSOI CMOS process. The on-wafer measurement shows wideband performance such as insertion loss less than 3 dB up to 21.5 GHz. The return loss is better than 10 dB up to 14.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact and Low-Cost THz SoP Heterogeneous Integration Platform
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A compact and low-cost THz system-on-package (SoP) heterogeneous integration platform is proposed in this work. Different chips fabricated in different technologies can be integrated together onto a common low-loss and low-cost integrated-passive-devices (IPD) carrier using low-loss chip-to-IPD THz interconnects. On-carrier low-loss microstrip lines, coplanar waveguides, and substrate-integrated waveguides (SIW) are used to communicate signals between these different chip modules. Low-loss SIW filters on the IPD carrier are employed to filter out undesired spurs, harmonics, noise, and interference signals. Experimental results show that the proposed single-band, dual-band, and broadband THz interconnects from a 0.18-$\mu$ m CMOS chip to an IPD carrier can give insertion loss of 2, 2.8 and 3.2 dB, and lower than 3.7 dB at 306.5, 140 and 324.5 GHz, and from 140 to 330 GHz, while keeping the return loss better than 10 dB from 256.5 to 330, 140 to 182 and 280 to 330, and 140 to 330 GHz, respectively. The measured insertion loss of a fourth-order Chebyshev SIW filter realized in a commercially-available GaAs IPD technology is 3.6 dB at 327.5 GHz. With the proposed THz heterogeneous integration platform, the unique advantages of these different chip modules realized in different technologies can be utilized to carry out compact, high-performance, low-cost, and high-integration THz systems for sensing and communication applications.

articleTitle: Design of a Coplanar Waveguide for X-band Radar Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a coplanar waveguide (CPW) layer for X-band radar antennas. The proposed CPW has three transition parts, which can minimize leakage electric fields and improve impedance matching characteristics of the CPW. To verify the feasibility, the CPW in the back-to-back configuration is fabricated, and the CPW performance such as the reflection and transmission coefficients are measured. The reflection coefficients are under -22 dB, and transmission coefficients are higher than -0.7 dB in the target frequency of 9 to 10 GHz. The results demonstrate that the proposed CPW can be applied to X-band radar applications.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Partial Denture Management RFID System Using a Simple Phantom Model
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We had proposed a 920MHz/5.02GHz dual-use RFID system to detect the existence of partial dentures for both in-body/out-body conditions. In this paper, the communication range has been measured for in-body RFID communication at 920MHz by using a simple phantom model. The partial denture with RFID has been placed at 3 different points in the oral cavity of the phantom model. Communication range of 200mm from the surface of phantom has been obtained for almost all around the phantom. Whereas, we have had no response from the RFID tag implanted in the denture at all position in the phantom at 5.02GHz. We’ve also confirmed the response from the RFID tag when the partial denture is placed out-body at 5.02GHz. These results show the feasibility to distinguish whether the partial denture with dual-use RFID tag is in-body or out-body.

articleTitle: Study of an Atmospheric Refractivity Estimation Using AREPS and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an estimation method of an atmospheric refractivity according to altitude. To estimate the atmospheric refractivity, an artificial trilinear model that can express the ducting conditions is applied to a genetic algorithm (GA) process. The calculated clutter power spectrum using the designed trilinear model is then compared with the calculated clutter power spectrum based on the measured atmospheric refractivity data. The result demonstrates that the atmospheric refractivity can be predicted using the proposed method from the sea clutter powers.

articleTitle: Body-Coupled Powering for Wearables
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Providing power to body-worn sensors and nodes is challenging. Energy Harvesting (EH) often faces source-destination location mismatch issues. Batteries are bulky and lead to “battery anxiety” as the number of nodes increases. Body-Coupled Power (BCP) Transfer and Energy Harvesting, on the other hand, uses the human body as a coupling medium to effectively distribute power on/around the human body. With the BCP, energy harvesters can be used without location constraints, and a single power source can provide power to multiple wearables around the body.

articleTitle: Microwave and Millimeter-wave Signal Generation using Injection Locked Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: High-speed clock generator is crucial for high-speed wireless/wire transmission, and it usually have some features of low phase noise, low jitter, low dc power consumption, and multi-phase outputs. In this paper, several advanced techniques are introduced for generating millimeter-wave and terahertz (THz) signal, such as multi-phase voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO), phase-locked loop (PLL), and sub-harmonically injection-locked methods. A few self-aligned techniques, including sub-harmonically injection-locked PLL (SILPLL) and frequency-locked loop (SILFLL), are presented to overcome the variations of the process, voltage, and temperature. Due to the self-aligned techniques, the SILPLL and SILFLL demonstrate excellent performance and good robustness. Furthermore, some advanced digital modulation signals, such as n-level quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) and orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), are generated using the injection-locked methods for the modern 5G applications.

articleTitle: Tabbed Routing Modeling and Design Optimization for High-speed Signaling Channel
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Recently, for the memory signaling channel, the data rate is getting increased up to 4.8 Gbps which can occur signal integrity issues such as insertion loss, far-end crosstalk, and time-domain reflectometer (TDR) mismatching. Thus, the tabbed routing pattern is introduced by Intel. In this paper, the tabbed routing modeling is introduced for design optimization of tabbed routing.

articleTitle: A 38 GHz Ultra-Compact High Power Density CMOS Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A fully-integrated 38 GHz power amplifier (PA) is presented on the 65 nm CMOS process. Utilizing broadside coupled half-turn transformer, the CMOS PA achieves high power density within an ultra-compact chip area. The experimental results show that the CMOS PA demonstrates a small-signal gain of 16.4 dB at 38 GHz. The measured saturation output power (Psat) is 20.2 dBm, an output 1-dB compression point (OP1dB) is 15 dBm, and the peak power-added-efficiency (PAE) is 28.8% at 38 GHz. The core area of the CMOS PA is 0.147 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the power density is 712 mW/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. For high speed digital modulation signal test, the PA transmits 9.5 dBm linear output power at -25dBc error vector magnitude (EVM) for a 1600-MHz channel bandwidth 64-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signal with data rate of 6.98 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Potential of Terahertz Communication Not Limited to Short Range
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Terahertz communications are expected to be used in the 6th generation communications and beyond, as data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s can be expected in wireless communications. On the other hand, it has been believed that the communication distance is limited to a short distance because the propagation loss increases as the frequency increases. This paper clarifies the relationship between carrier frequency and propagation distance. We also show that, under the right conditions, long-distance communication can be expected even with terahertz communication. We also discuss the hardware requirements for such long-distance communication.

articleTitle: An 87% Efficient Wireless Powered System Using Adaptively Controlled Active Rectifier for Smart Electronics
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This brief presents an efficient wireless powered system (WPS) for smart electronics, including battery charging. To enhance the performance of WPS, we have utilized an adaptively-controlled active rectifier matrix (AARM) that helps to regulate the output voltage over a wide-range load variation. In addition, we propose a digital compensation circuit that adjusts both turn-on and turn-off times to compensate for delays of the comparator when it turns off and on. The proposed WPS is implemented in a 0.18 $\mu$m high-voltage Bipolar-CMOS-DMOS(BCD) process. The WPS can achieve 270 mW of the peak (a) power while flowing 135 mA of the load current. The measured peak conversion efficiency is S7% at 0. 89mW of the output power.

articleTitle: A High PAE Stacked K-band Power Amplifier Using π-Phase Compensation Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A three-tunable low-pass π-phase compensator technique is proposed and employed in a K-band CMOS power amplifier (PA) to solve the phase shift problem at intermediate nodes of stacked transistor configurations (STCs). Also, it reduces the effects of harmonic signals that in turns, enhances the overall power added efficiency (PAE) of the PA. The PA consists of two stages i.e. driver and main stages, designed using 2-STCs in 180-nm CMOS technology. The fabricated PA achieved a power gain of 12.8 dB at 23 GHz, a maximum PAE of 18.3%, an output power of 1 dB compression point $\left(\mathrm{P}_{1 \mathrm{~dB}}\right)$ of 14.1 1 dBm, and saturated output power $\left(\mathrm{P}_{\text {sat }}\right)$ of 16.0 dBm while it consumes chip area of 0.604 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> including pads.

articleTitle: Emerging Computing Systems Utilizing Electro-Magnetic Near-Field Connectivity
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper introduces technology directions of next-generation emerging computer systems utilizing electro-magnetic near-field connectivity around IC chips. We will discuss the potential advantages of this technology in demonstrations of 1) high-bandwidth low-cost wireless interconnections for vertically-stacked 3D ICs, wireless power and data links for non-contact ICs, and electro-magnetic disturbance sensors for secure IC against physical attacks.

articleTitle: A Wearable Oscillator Tag for Heart Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents a chest-worn oscillator tag for monitoring the heart health of an exercising person without direct contact with the skin. The tag operates at 5.8 GHz based on the self-injection-locking (SIL) Doppler radar principle and consists mainly of an oscillator and an antenna. For validation, a heart health monitoring system was developed with the proposed tag to detect the cardiac intervals of a wearer who performs various activities including walking and running. The results thus obtained agree closely with electrocardiogram (ECG) measurements.

articleTitle: RF Front-End Transmitting System for Agricultural Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: In this paper, a design of an RF front-end transmitter for actuating greenhouse plant leaves with electromagnetic wave is proposed. The proposed RF front-end transmitter consists of a phase-locked loop (PLL), variable attenuator, power amplifier (PA), protector and detector circuits, and antenna. The overall circuit is designed for ISM band application with a center frequency of 2.45 GHz. The attenuation range of the variable attenuator is 20 dB. This variable attenuator is connected between PLL and driver PA to control the radiated electromagnetic wave power level for the optimum plant growing condition. The RF power higher than 20 W can be obtained at the output port of PA. The protector and detector circuits consist of the isolator, dual directional coupler, and RF detecting circuits. The isolator is used to protect the PA from the reflected power when the antenna is disconnected from the system. The RF detecting circuits are connected to the couple ports of the dual directional coupler to check long time operation. The designed PAs have been operated very well on humid operating conditions for 14 days.

articleTitle: A 19GHz 5-Bit Low RMS Phase Error Passive Phase Shifter Using 0.18μm CMOS Process
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 19 GHz 5-bit low root mean square (RMS) phase error passive phase shifter using $0.18\mu\mathrm{m}$ CMOS technology is presented in this paper. A biphase switching reflection-type based topology is applied to the 90° and 180° phase-shift bits. The 5-bit phase shifter demonstrates the lowest RMS phase error of 1.67° at 19 GHz with an intrinsic digital phase-control mechanism. The RMS phase error is less than 4° from 16 to 23 GHz. The measured insertion loss is 16 ± 2 dB from 16 to 23 GHz over all 32 states.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Low Integrated-Phase-Noise 28-GHz LO Generator for 5G Transceivers Supporting Multiple Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This work presents a multi-band LO generator that concurrently can support existing cellular bands below 6 GHz and new millimeter-wave (mmW) bands for 5G. Using a low-noise reference-frequency doubler, a $\Delta \Sigma$ fractional-N phase-locked loop (PLL) generates GHz-range signals with low integrated phase noise (IPN). Then, injection-locked frequency multipliers increase these frequencies to mmW bands without degrading IPN. The proposed LO-generator was fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process. When the PLL is in the fractional-N mode, the measured IPN and RMS jitter integrated from 1 kHz to 100 MHz of the 29.23-GHz signal were −31.4 dBc and 206 fs, respectively. When the PLL is in the integer-N mode, the measured IPN and RMS jitter of the 28.8-GHz signal were −33.1 dBc and 172 fs, respectively. The silicon area was 0.95 mm$^{\mathbf{2}}$, and the total power consumption was 36.4 mW.

articleTitle: 26 GHz 2-Stacked Power Amplifier Using 28 nm Bulk CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 26 GHz differential 2-stacked power amplifier (PA) with L-C and C-L second-harmonic termination circuits was designed using 28 nm bulk CMOS process. To improve both gain and stability, neutralization using a cross-coupled capacitor was adopted. The implemented PAIC exhibited a gain of 11.9 dB, a power-added efficiency (PAE) of 25.6%, a drain efficiency (DE) of 31.1%, and a saturated output power of 17.1 dBm using a CW excitation. A wide bandwidth of 5 GHz was obtained. The fabricated PAIC has an active area of 0.152 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Frequency Discrimination Based on the Different Number of Peaks in Envelope Detection of Two-Tone CW Radar
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A method for distinguishing the baseband signal for each frequency in two-tone radar is proposed by using the difference in the number of peaks of the envelope detected signal. The proposed method is based on the characteristic that the baseband signal for each frequency has a different number of peaks depending on the operating frequency at the fixed sampling frequency in data acquisition. The phase difference between the transmitting and receiving signals for each frequency can be obtained by using envelope detection of the baseband signals in the two-tone radar, and the proposed method can effectively match the phase difference and the operating frequency without using additional control and synchronization. This makes it simple to estimate the absolute range up to the maximum unambiguous range, corresponding to a phase difference of 2 $\pi$. Measurement results show that the absolute range using the two-tone radar with a frequency spacing of 150 MHz can detect the distance with an accuracy of 97.8% up to the maximum unambiguous range by using the proposed method.

articleTitle: Terahertz 3D Imaging with a 300-GHz CMOS Multi-Chip Array Detector
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A 300-GHz 4×4 multi-chip detector array based on a 65-nm CMOS technology has been developed and successfully applied to 3D terahertz imaging. The detector array with a modular assembly consists of 16 single-chip detector arrays in 4×4 format, each single chip including 7×7 unit pixels. The resultant large pixel count of 971 (including the virtual pixels) with the multi-chip array allows single-shot 2D images without raster scan, enabling a rapid 3D terahertz imaging with a significantly reduced acquisition time. In this work, 3D images of a metallic bolt were successfully acquired at 300 GHz with the image setup that employs the developed multi-chip array as the detector.

articleTitle: 150-GHz Vector Modulator Phase Shifter in 65-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: A D-band vector modulator-type phase shifter (VMPS) is presented using a 65-nm CMOS process. The proposed VMPS is based on a single Gilbert cell configuration to reduce insertion loss and minimize the effects of the parasitic components. Quadrature signals are generated from the Lange coupler with low insertion loss. A D-band output signal is generated from the vector summation from the quadrature signals controlled with the gate bias of the Gilbert cell. The output transformer is designed to simultaneously achieve low loss combining in the quadrature signals and impedance matching. In the EM-circuit co-simulation results, the proposed VMPS, implemented on the size 0.4 × 0.47 mm2 including all pads, shows that a gain of −12.5(±3) dB and an input P1dB of 7 dBm with a power consumption of 15.7 mW at the operating frequency of 150 GHz.

articleTitle: Chip-Level High-Frequency EMC Strategies and Measurement Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: This paper presents different electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) strategies for achieving low EM emission and high immunity. The proposed designs and measurement techniques for improving and evaluating the chip level EM interference (EMI) and EM susceptibility (EMS) are included to provide high-frequency EMC solutions. This paper also gives a comprehensive overview for the researchers to continue working on the EMC-related topics and issues at the chip level at high frequencies.

articleTitle: Fast Anomaly Detection via the Orthogonality Sampling Method in Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: We consider an application of the orthogonality sampling method (OSM) for a fast identification of a small anomaly from scattering parameter data. In this study, we cannot measure the scattering parameter data when the location of transmitting and receiving antenna is same. Due to this reason, we set the unknown data as a constant and design a new indicator function of the OSM with multiple sources weighted by the incident field data. Based on the simulation results, we confirmed that the designed indicator function improves the imaging quality successfully.

articleTitle: A 260GHz Wireless Transmission over 100m for Beyond 5G Xhaul Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Beyond 5G networks require ultra-high data-rate, moderate-distance, scalable and cost-effective Xhaul (fronthaul/ mid-haul/backhaul) networks. It is expected that some of the current optical fiber based Xhaul links will be replaced by millimeter-wave based ones if the wireless data throughput performance exceeds 100Gbps over 100m distance. In this paper, we present a sub-THz ($250 \sim 270$ GHz) RF system design and measurement result including channel characteristics for future wireless Xhaul networks. Design issues of terahertz band RF components such as high-gain antenna, power amplifier and ADC data converters are provided. In addition, this paper highlights the demonstration of wireless data transmission performed while moving the unit mounted on the top of the vehicle to a distance of 100m and more from the Road Side Unit.

articleTitle: Modeling of Hot-Via Technology for System-in-Package at Millimeter-wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Hot via technology plays an important role for system integration at millimeter-wave frequencies. Accurate prediction of the parasitics is necessary to ensure proper impedance matching for system applications. In this paper, we report the characterization of hot-via interconnect for system-in-package (SiP) applications at millimeter-wave frequencies. A test structure using microstrip to grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) transition has been characterized to extract the equivalent circuit model of the hot-via. The model demonstrates an excellent agreement with measurements up to 50 GHz.

articleTitle: 140 GHz Silicon I/O Interconnect Exploiting Metadevices for Short-Range OOK Communications
publicationTitle: 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Radio-Frequency Integration Technology (RFIT)
abstract: Wide bandwidth and low-power on-chip interconnects are increasingly in demand for high-speed data communication in future exascale computer servers. While CMOS technologies continue to scale in size and improve their performance in terms of operating frequency and speed, the overall system performance is limited by other figures of merit, such as the interconnect between circuits, power consumption, and signal integrity.Recently, optical, radio-frequency (RF), and baseband (BB) I/O transceivers are reported. The optical interconnects have shown good energy efficiency with reconfigurable capability, but it is difficult to be fully integrated in CMOS technology. Particularly, it requires extra cost on packaging. Baseband transceivers can be fully integrated on chip. Unfortunately, as data rates increase, the RC (or LC) time delay, IR voltage drop, and $CV^{2}f$ power loss, as well as channel crosstalk become dominating. In contrast to BB signaling, the RF interconnect transmits electromagnetic (EM)-wave signal in the channel. The binary data of “0” and “1” can be distinguished via OOK modulation. Yet, the data throughput is limited by the narrowband at RF and thus making the data rate to be limited at ∼10 Gb/s. Such a shortcoming has been recently tackled by utilizing carriers at much higher frequencies. Called terahertz (THz)-interconnect, the data rate has been boosted beyond 20 Gb/s, but this approach suffers from significant channel crosstalk as well as small ON/OFF ratio of modulator. Unfortunately, the degradation on the bit-error rate due to the above two factors have not been fully addressed by the prior arts.This talk reports three metadevices for addressing the above challenges for THz-interconnects. The surface plasmonic polariton (SPP), which is commonly recognized with negative permittivity behavior, has demonstrated orders of crosstalk attenuation because its electrical field (E-field) exponentially decays perpendicularly to the metal interface. By gradually corrugating periodical subwavelength metal strips onto the traditional transmission line, SPPs are excited on chip with impedance and mode matching with traditional TEM devices. With this concept, more than 20 dB channel crosstalk suppression has been realized at W-band when the plasmonic channel spacing is $2.4 \mu \mathrm{m}$. In addition, a split-ring resonator (SRR)-based modulator is introduced. Owing to its high quality-factor, the SRR's resonance is strong inside the ring slit, leading to possibility that attains a high ON/OFF ratio by manipulating the resonance state of the SRR. Incorporating four CMOS switches into the SRR, the SRR can transit its characteristic between passband and stopband, and thus enables amplitude modulation without consuming static power. The SRR-based modulator achieves a recorded 40 dB ON/OFF ratio, occupying only 0.002 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area. Third, a four-way power-combined coupled-oscillator-network (CON) is introduced. It takes advantages of both SRR and plasmonic transmission line for high-Q resonance, as well as synchronizing each oscillator unit-cell in a close loop. The CON delivers maximum 5.6 dBm at W-band. Finally, a dual-channel plasmonic I/O transceiver is reported. Utilizing the above three metadevices, the proposed fully-integrated 140-GHz I/O can communicate 13.5 Gb/s/lane OOK data stream with $\le 10^{-12}$ BER and 2.6-pJ/bit/lane energy efficiency, demonstrating crosstalk-immune feature for THz-interconnect. In contrast, the recovered eye of traditional I/O transceiver are fully distorted due to the channel crosstalk. This work paves a new way toward highly-efficient I/O interconnect for future big-data exascale parallel computing.
